claim: Which base and residue the GRCh37 reference carries at SLC19A1 c.80 / residue 27, and therefore which direction the coding shorthand in methylation_panel.json must run to agree with the row's own p.His27Arg. No biological, statistical or clinical claim is asserted; in particular no claim is made about which rs1051266 allele affects folate transport, and the row's risk/ref dosage pair, genotype_effects categories and evidence level are unchanged.

high_stakes_two_source_rule: Engaged and satisfied, after a correction. The reference-base claim is carried in a durable artifact (the rendered panel label), so it needs two agreeing sources that share neither a dataset nor an assertion chain. An earlier version of this packet named NCBI dbSNP and Ensembl GRCh37 as the two; that was WRONG, because the retained Ensembl response declares its own source as 'Variants (including SNPs and indels) imported from dbSNP', so the two share an upstream. The independent pair is instead NCBI RefSeq/dbSNP (NM_194255.4/NP_919231.1) and UniProtKB P41440, which is curated by the UniProt consortium from EMBL/GenBank/DDBJ translations and the literature rather than from dbSNP, and which establishes the reference RESIDUE (His at position 27) directly rather than by way of the variant record. Ensembl is retained as corroboration and as the source of ancestral-allele and frequency context, not as an independent vote. The His->Arg = A->G step itself is the standard genetic code and is not sourced.

queries.derived_extract_rule: Retains identity, merge status and every NM_194255.4 placement with its NP_919231.1 protein consequence. Kept for readability only; the source-native 250974-byte response is retained in full alongside it, so any selection or transcription can be checked.
queries.result_used: rs1051266 is not merged. NM_194255.4:c.80= maps to NP_919231.1 residue 27 H->H, establishing His as the reference residue; NM_194255.4:c.80A>G maps to residue 27 H->R as a missense_variant. The same transcript also carries c.80A>C (H->P) and c.80A>T (H->L), so dbSNP records THREE alternates and the record is four-allelic (A reference plus G, C, T). Ensembl's GRCh37 allele_string is narrower at T/C/G, i.e. two alternates; the packet reports both rather than reconciling them. Either way, A>G is one alternate among several and not 'the' alternate.
queries.supports: A80G (His27Arg) is the reference-frame spelling; G80A is not.

queries.field_selection_note: The request itself selected accession, id, sequence, protein name, gene names and sequence version. The response is retained exactly as returned; no post-hoc editing was applied.
queries.result_used: P41440 (S19A1_HUMAN), Reduced folate transporter, gene SLC19A1, canonical sequence 591 aa, CRC64 0437B1615F5517EB. Residues 20-35 are PELRSWRHLVCYLCFY, so residue 27 is H (His).
queries.supports: Independent confirmation that the reference residue at position 27 is His, hence p.His27Arg and not p.Arg27His. This is the second source for the high-stakes rule.

queries.result_used: chr21:46,957,794 plus strand, allele_string T/C/G, ancestral_allele C, minor_allele C at MAF 0.4886. SLC19A1 is on the minus strand, so plus-strand T is coding A (reference) and plus-strand C is coding G. Note this lists two alternates where dbSNP lists three; the two sources disagree on the allele count and this packet does not resolve that.
queries.supports: Corroboration only, NOT an independent vote: the response declares its own source as variants imported from dbSNP, so it shares an upstream with the RefSNP record. Retained for its allele string, the ancestral allele and the frequency.

corroborating_query.description: Same committed bundle joined against the committed tests/fixtures/seed_csvs/vep_seed.csv on (rsid, pos). The recorded statement matches on (rsid, pos) ALONE; the orientation split below then applies a further filter on the unordered allele pair, which the SQL does not express.
corroborating_query.sql: select ref,alt,hgvs_protein,strand from vep_annotations where rsid=? and pos=?;
corroborating_query.why_26_are_excluded: Orientation is undefined when the two sources do not name the same two alleles, so those 26 cannot be scored as agreeing or reversed and are counted separately rather than dropped silently. They differ by more than orientation - some are strand complements (rs5026665 seed T/C vs bundle A/G), others name a different alternate entirely (rs913722 seed A/T vs bundle C/T; rs7601387 seed A/T vs bundle A/G). They are a further discrepancy class between the two artifacts and are NOT evidence for the alphabetical-ordering finding, which rests on the 102254/102254 count above.
corroborating_query.result: 44 matched; 12 same orientation, 6 reversed, 26 different allele pair, 635 absent.

source_versions_and_licenses._why: Recording the version/build and licence basis for every source, so a future auditor can establish which source state produced each retained payload and on what basis retaining it is permitted.

NCBI dbSNP RefSNP v2.version_or_build: The response carries the RefSNP's own last_update_build_id and dates; the 2026-08-10 access date bounds retrieval. No API version beyond the v0 path segment is issued.
NCBI dbSNP RefSNP v2.license_or_terms: US Government work produced by the National Library of Medicine; NCBI databases are in the public domain in the United States.
NCBI dbSNP RefSNP v2.retention_basis: Public domain. Only variant metadata for a single rsID is retained; no human subject data is involved.

UniProtKB P41440.version_or_build: Canonical sequence identified by CRC64 0437B1615F5517EB and length 591. The field-selected response did not return an entry or sequence version number, so the CRC64 plus the 2026-08-10 access date is the version boundary asserted here; no numeric version is claimed.
UniProtKB P41440.license_or_terms: UniProt data are distributed under CC BY 4.0.
UniProtKB P41440.retention_basis: CC BY 4.0 permits redistribution with attribution, and the source is attributed by accession. Only the canonical protein record is retained.
unavailable_fields: sequence version number (not returned by the field-selected response)

Ensembl GRCh37 REST.version_or_build: GRCh37 archive endpoint. The response carries no release number, so the 2026-08-10 access date is the retrieval-version boundary. The GRCh37 site is a frozen mirror and lags current dbSNP, which is why dbSNP rather than Ensembl is the primary source for identity and merge status.
Ensembl GRCh37 REST.license_or_terms: Ensembl data are released under the Apache License 2.0.
Ensembl GRCh37 REST.retention_basis: Apache 2.0 permits redistribution with attribution. Only the single-rsID variation record is retained.

Consensus and Scite.version_or_build: Neither service exposes a corpus version; the 2026-08-10 access date is the boundary.
Consensus and Scite.license_or_terms: Only the outcome of each query is retained in prose - which spellings appear in titles/abstracts, and whether an editorial notice exists. No abstract or full text is reproduced beyond short bibliographic identification.

PMID:16750224 / PMID:24597986 / PMID:339.version_or_build: Version of record. These are the three citations already carried by the panel row; only their titles and editorial-notice status are used here.
PMID:16750224 / PMID:24597986 / PMID:339.license_or_terms: Titles only, used as bibliographic fact. No abstract or full text is retained or reproduced.
PMID:16750224 / PMID:24597986 / PMID:339.retention_basis: Bibliographic metadata, attributed by PMID and DOI.
